title: Frontend Developer: Mid-level screening (SAMPLE, dev only)
description: Sample content for testing the library picker. Replace with reviewed content before launch.

questions.questionText: A page renders a list of 5,000 rows and scrolling is janky. Which change most directly reduces the work the browser does while the user scrolls?
options: Wrap every row component in React.memo to skip re-renders
Inline the row styles to avoid stylesheet lookups
Virtualize the list so only visible rows are in the DOM
Use array indexes as keys so React reuses DOM nodes
questions.correctAnswer: Virtualize the list so only visible rows are in the DOM

questions.questionText: A component starts a setInterval inside a useEffect with an empty dependency array and logs count every second. The logged value never changes even though the UI updates. What is the cause?
options: The interval callback captured the first render's count
setInterval callbacks run before React commits state
Empty dependency arrays make state updates asynchronous
React drops state updates that happen inside timers
questions.correctAnswer: The interval callback captured the first render's count

questions.questionText: Which element should a control that submits a form be, so keyboard and screen reader users get the right behaviour without extra ARIA?
options: A div with role="button" and an onClick handler
An anchor with href="#" and an onClick handler
A span with tabindex="0" and an onClick handler
A button element with type="submit"

questions.questionText: A signed-in user requests an API route that only admins may use. Which HTTP status is the most accurate response?
options: 401 Unauthorized
403 Forbidden
404 Not Found
409 Conflict

questions.questionText: A comment field is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML and the comment text comes straight from other users. What is the main risk?
options: Stored cross-site scripting if the HTML is not sanitized
SQL injection against the comments table
Cross-site request forgery on the comment form
Exposing the API key in the page source
questions.correctAnswer: Stored cross-site scripting if the HTML is not sanitized

questions.questionText:
The rules ".card p { color: blue }" and "p.note { color: red }" both match

inside .card, with equal specificity. Which colour does the paragraph get?
options: Blue, because the first rule is more specific
Red, because it names the element and its class directly
Whichever rule appears later in the stylesheet
Neither, the browser inherits the parent colour
questions.correctAnswer: Whichever rule appears later in the stylesheet

questions.questionText: Using await inside the callback passed to Array.prototype.forEach makes the loop wait, so each iteration finishes before the next starts.
options: True
False

questions.questionText: In a component test, a button appears only after data loads from an API. Which approach is the most reliable way to assert it appears?
options: Wait one second with setTimeout, then call getByRole
Read the component's state through its instance
Await findByRole, which retries until it appears or times out
Snapshot the first render and compare it later
questions.correctAnswer: Await findByRole, which retries until it appears or times out

questions.questionText: Items in a list can be reordered and deleted by the user. Which value is the best React key for each item?
options: The item's index in the array
A random number generated on every render
The item's visible text
A stable id that comes with the item's data
questions.correctAnswer: A stable id that comes with the item's data
